implementation.policy: Restore on ordinary no-argument startup; skip explicit open intents, CMUX_DISABLE_SESSION_RESTORE, CMUX_UI_TEST_* environments, and XCTest environments.
implementation.state_rules: Load current with previous fallback, rotate the snapshot, prune nonrestorable/crash state, cap at 12 windows, normalize identities, create additional native windows, roll back on runtime failure, restore active selection, and persist the live result.

gates: cargo test -p cmux-desktop --test session_startup_restore_process: passed before and after simplification

canonical_verification.termination_contract: Terminate the exact app PID through NSRunningApplication.terminate so canonical applicationShouldTerminate performs its synchronous session write before relaunch.

runs.error: swiftc required -parse-as-library for the @main termination helper; canonical did not launch

canonical_verification.observed: Canonical restored two windows, retained the target workspace as selected, retained three target surfaces, and restored surface:6 as focused.

behavioral_deltas: Canonical preserves the first restored window as window:1; Windows exposes it as window:3 in window.list.
The unscoped post-restore workspace.list routes to selected window:2 on canonical but window:1 on Windows.
Canonical target surface order is surface:5, surface:6, surface:4; Windows order is surface:4, surface:5, surface:6. Both focus surface:6.
The state lane also contains unapproved platform/runtime payload differences in working directories, terminal titles, and remote-detail fields.

promotion_decision.reason: Both platforms restore the two-window fixture, but the exact comparison has one state-lane delta with unexplained window-ref continuity, default routing, and target surface-order differences.
